title: Kalev speaks to the iron and takes the apprentice

approval.notes: ADR 0052 opening, beat 3 (rewrites the SD-05 forge version): Kalev comes to the almshouse sickbed, finds his own mark on the broken spearhead (flag.prologue.saw_makers_mark, a lead for quest.makers_mark), speaks the origin-of-iron charm while the boy holds Lambert, notices that the boy sees, and takes him in (flag.prologue.apprenticed). Entry variants open on the calming duel's ending.

nodes.text: I heard him from the lane, screaming at shadows. Whatever you said to him, say no more. Only hold him.
He lies quiet. Gertrud said he fought the linen all evening. Good, boy.
Gertrud, the lamp. Water and clean linen. Let me see the iron.
...That socket came off my anvil. It bears my mark.

choices.text: You made the spear that did this?

nodes.text: I made spearheads for the watch. Not for this. Later. Hold his shoulders, boy, and do not let go.
Iron, I know your birth. You lay in the bog as red rust, under the wolf's track, under the bear's paw.
You were not great then, you were not proud. The smith took you from the mire and gave you an edge. Why do you bite your brother?
Go back the way you came. Blood, stand like a wall, stand like a fence of stones, like reeds in still water.
There. It is out, and he still breathes. Press the linen, boy. Harder.
You were watching his side when I came in. Not the blood. Something over it.

choices.text: There was something over him. It was afraid.

nodes.text: You saw where it hurt him before I touched him. Come to the forge tonight, when Gertrud lets you go. Mart's bed is empty.

source_notes.summary: Kalev's origin-of-iron charm (nodes kalev_charm_birth, kalev_charm_shame, kalev_charm_blood) is a plausible composite after the Baltic-Finnic 'birth of iron' charm type spoken over iron wounds (Finnish Raudan synty, Estonian raua sõnad; collected centuries after 1343, no 1343 text survives), with a common stop-the-blood formula; rendered in English. The smith as healer is plausible composite (ADR 0052).
Kalev's lines, the almshouse sickbed scene and the spearhead with his mark are authored for the ADR 0052 opening.
